newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends lower due to U.S. weakness.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends lower due to U.S. weakness.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures ended weaker on Monday after the U.S. heating oil market came under pressure, traders said.
January gas oil stood $2.50 a tonne weaker, having settled the day's session at $229.50. February Brent was two cents up on the day at $24.58 a barrel at 1805 GMT.
"Gas oil is off on the back of (NYMEX) heating oil," one dealer said. "Brent is really following the States too."
NYMEX heating oil futures for February were 0.74 cents a gallon down at 72.90 cents.

But IPE dealers said that business was very lacklustre, adding that icy conditions in Europe were hampering canal traffic into Europe, and this had contributed to the downside move on gas oil futures.

Traders were awaiting the release late on Tuesday of weekly data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) and U.S. traders earlier said they were expecting a build in middle distillate stocks of up to three million barrels.
